quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: The woman who is standing by the door is my aunt. Which of these means exactly the same thing, in reduced form?
quests.targetClause: The woman standing by the door is my aunt.
quests.completedSentence: The woman who is standing by the door is my aunt. Which of these means exactly the same thing, in reduced form?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Standing' is the reduced form of 'who is standing': the subject relative pronoun and the auxiliary 'is' are dropped, leaving just the present participle.
quests.nativeTip: Drop both the relative pronoun and the verb 'is,' keeping only the '-ing' form.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The woman standing by the door is my aunt."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Full: 'The passengers who were waiting at the gate grew impatient.' Reduced: 'The passengers ___ at the gate grew impatient.'
quests.targetClause: waiting
quests.completedSentence: Full: 'The passengers who were waiting at the gate grew impatient.' Reduced: 'The passengers waiting at the gate grew impatient.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Waiting' is correct: it reduces 'who were waiting,' dropping the pronoun and the auxiliary 'were,' leaving the present participle.
quests.nativeTip: The full clause describes an ongoing action ('were waiting') - which participle captures that?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "waiting"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence can be correctly reduced using an '-ing' form?
quests.targetClause: The chef who is preparing the tasting menu trained in Paris.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence can be correctly reduced using an '-ing' form?
quests.ruleExplanation: Only subject relative clauses reduce with '-ing': the chef is doing the preparing. In the other case, 'I' is doing the preparing, not 'the dish,' so that object relative clause cannot be reduced this way.
quests.nativeTip: Check who is doing the preparing in each sentence - is the antecedent itself performing the action?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The chef who is preparing the tasting menu trained in Paris."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: The car that was stolen last night was found this morning. Which of these means exactly the same thing, in reduced form?
quests.targetClause: The car stolen last night was found this morning.
quests.completedSentence: The car that was stolen last night was found this morning. Which of these means exactly the same thing, in reduced form?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Stolen' is the reduced form of 'that was stolen': the pronoun and the auxiliary 'was' are dropped, leaving just the past participle - correct because the original clause was passive.
quests.nativeTip: Drop both the relative pronoun and the verb 'was,' keeping only the past participle.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The car stolen last night was found this morning."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Full: 'The documents that were signed yesterday need to be filed.' Reduced: 'The documents ___ yesterday need to be filed.'
quests.targetClause: signed
quests.completedSentence: Full: 'The documents that were signed yesterday need to be filed.' Reduced: 'The documents signed yesterday need to be filed.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Signed' is correct: it reduces 'that were signed,' dropping the pronoun and 'were,' leaving the past participle.
quests.nativeTip: The full clause is passive ('were signed') - which participle matches a passive meaning?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "signed"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence correctly uses a reduced clause to show that the report was WRITTEN BY someone else?
quests.targetClause: The report written by the intern contained several errors.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence correctly uses a reduced clause to show that the report was WRITTEN BY someone else?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Written' (past participle) correctly shows the passive meaning; '-ing' would incorrectly suggest the report itself is actively writing something.
quests.nativeTip: The report didn't write itself - someone wrote it. Which participle form shows this passive relationship correctly?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The report written by the intern contained several errors."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Compare: A) 'The employee managing the project...' B) 'The employee managed by the project...' Which one describes an employee who is IN CHARGE of the project?
quests.targetClause: Sentence A
quests.completedSentence: Compare: A) 'The employee managing the project...' B) 'The employee managed by the project...' Which one describes an employee who is IN CHARGE of the project?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Managing' shows the employee is doing the managing - in charge of the project. 'Managed by the project' would be an odd passive, since projects don't typically manage people.
quests.nativeTip: Ask whether the employee is performing the managing, or receiving it - and whether that second reading even makes sense.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "Sentence A"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: The negotiations ___ by both sides finally reached a resolution.
quests.targetClause: led
quests.completedSentence: The negotiations led by both sides finally reached a resolution.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Led' is correct because the negotiations were led BY both sides - a passive relationship; '-ing' would wrongly suggest the negotiations themselves were actively leading something.
quests.nativeTip: Were the negotiations doing the leading, or being led by the two sides?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "led"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence correctly describes a student who FEELS curious about the topic, rather than one who causes curiosity in others?
quests.targetClause: The interested student asked several follow-up questions.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence correctly describes a student who FEELS curious about the topic, rather than one who causes curiosity in others?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Interested' describes the student's own feeling. 'Interesting' would describe a student who causes interest in others - a different meaning entirely.
quests.nativeTip: One of these participles describes how the student feels; the other describes the effect the student has on other people.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The interested student asked several follow-up questions."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence CANNOT be correctly reduced using a participle?
quests.targetClause: The pictures that the photographer is taking will be ready tomorrow.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence CANNOT be correctly reduced using a participle?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The photographer' - not 'the pictures' - is doing the taking, so this is an object relative clause; object relative clauses generally cannot be reduced to a simple participle this way, unlike subject relative clauses.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether the antecedent is doing the action, or receiving it from someone else mentioned in the clause.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The pictures that the photographer is taking will be ready tomorrow."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence sounds unnatural if reduced with an '-ing' form, because the verb describes a mental state rather than an ongoing action?
quests.targetClause: The man who knows the answer raised his hand.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence sounds unnatural if reduced with an '-ing' form, because the verb describes a mental state rather than an ongoing action?
quests.ruleExplanation: Stative verbs like 'know,' 'believe,' or 'want' generally resist this kind of reduction, even though the '-ing' form technically exists; 'waiting' reduces naturally, but 'knowing' sounds stiff or archaic here.
quests.nativeTip: Compare 'waiting,' which describes an ongoing action, with 'knowing,' which describes a mental state - does the second sound natural in everyday speech?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The man who knows the answer raised his hand."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence CANNOT be reduced to a shorter participle phrase?
quests.targetClause: The employee whose contract is being reviewed raised concerns.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence CANNOT be reduced to a shorter participle phrase?
quests.ruleExplanation: Clauses beginning with 'whose' generally cannot be shortened to a simple participle phrase, because 'whose' shows possession, not simply a subject doing or receiving an action.
quests.nativeTip: Reduction works by dropping a relative pronoun and a form of 'be' - does 'whose' behave the same way as 'who' or 'that' here?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The employee whose contract is being reviewed raised concerns."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Why can't 'The man whose car was stolen' be reduced to something like 'The man car stolen'?
quests.targetClause: Because dropping 'whose' would break the possessive link between the man and the car, leaving the sentence unclear.
quests.completedSentence: Why can't 'The man whose car was stolen' be reduced to something like 'The man car stolen'?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whose' shows that the car belongs to the man; removing it would destroy that link, leaving a nonsensical string of nouns. This differs from 'who' or 'that,' which can be dropped because the participle alone still shows the relationship to the antecedent.
quests.nativeTip: Think about what job 'whose' is doing in this sentence - what would be lost if it disappeared?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "Because dropping 'whose' would break the possessive link between the man and the car, leaving the sentence unclear."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence correctly keeps 'whose' unreduced, as required?
quests.targetClause: The company whose profits declined announced layoffs.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence correctly keeps 'whose' unreduced, as required?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whose' must stay to show that the profits belong to the company; none of the other options preserve both the meaning and the grammar.
quests.nativeTip: Only one of these keeps the possessive link between the company and its profits clear and grammatical.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The company whose profits declined announced layoffs."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: The company whose profits declined announced layoffs affecting workers across three states. Which part of this sentence IS a valid reduction?
quests.targetClause: affecting workers across three states
quests.completedSentence: The company whose profits declined announced layoffs affecting workers across three states. Which part of this sentence IS a valid reduction?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Affecting workers across three states' is a reduced form of 'that affected workers...' - a valid reduction, unlike the 'whose' clause earlier in the sentence, which must stay in full.
quests.nativeTip: Look for a participle phrase elsewhere in the sentence that stands in for a full relative clause, separate from the 'whose' clause.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "affecting workers across three states"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: My brother, who lives in Paris, works as a chef. Can this non-defining clause also be reduced?
quests.targetClause: Yes: 'My brother, living in Paris, works as a chef.'
quests.completedSentence: My brother, who lives in Paris, works as a chef. Can this non-defining clause also be reduced?
quests.ruleExplanation: Non-defining clauses can be reduced too, as long as the commas stay in place: 'living in Paris' replaces 'who lives in Paris,' with the extra information still clearly set off by commas.
quests.nativeTip: Try applying the same drop-the-pronoun-and-'be' pattern you've used before, but keep the commas this time.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "Yes: 'My brother, living in Paris, works as a chef.'"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: The bridge, which was built in 1932, connects the two districts. Which reduced version is correct?
quests.targetClause: The bridge, built in 1932, connects the two districts.
quests.completedSentence: The bridge, which was built in 1932, connects the two districts. Which reduced version is correct?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Built' correctly reduces 'which was built,' and the commas must stay since this is still non-defining information about a unique bridge.
quests.nativeTip: Keep the commas exactly where they were, and choose the participle form that matches the passive meaning of 'was built.'
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The bridge, built in 1932, connects the two districts."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence commits an error by losing its commas during reduction?
quests.targetClause: Mount Everest standing at over 8,800 meters is the tallest mountain on Earth.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence commits an error by losing its commas during reduction?
quests.ruleExplanation: Reducing a clause doesn't remove the need for its commas; since Mount Everest is unique, the non-defining comma must stay even in the reduced form.
quests.nativeTip: Ask whether 'Mount Everest' needs any narrowing down at all - and whether the comma should have stayed even after reduction.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "Mount Everest standing at over 8,800 meters is the tallest mountain on Earth."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: The team managing the crisis worked around the clock. What is the FULL, unreduced meaning of 'managing the crisis'?
quests.targetClause: who was managing the crisis / who were managing the crisis
quests.completedSentence: The team managing the crisis worked around the clock. What is the FULL, unreduced meaning of 'managing the crisis'?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Managing' is a present participle showing an active relationship: the team was doing the managing. The full form is 'who was/were managing the crisis.'
quests.nativeTip: Ask whether the team is doing the managing, or whether something else is managing the team.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "who was managing the crisis / who were managing the crisis"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: The employees selected for the pilot program will start Monday. What is the FULL, unreduced meaning of 'selected for the pilot program'?
quests.targetClause: who were selected for the pilot program
quests.completedSentence: The employees selected for the pilot program will start Monday. What is the FULL, unreduced meaning of 'selected for the pilot program'?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Selected' is a past participle showing a passive relationship: someone else selected the employees. The full form is 'who were selected for the pilot program.'
quests.nativeTip: Ask whether the employees chose the program, or whether someone else chose the employees for it.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "who were selected for the pilot program"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Compare: A) 'The horse racing down the track was disqualified.' B) 'The horse raced down the track was disqualified.' Which one means the horse itself was running?
quests.targetClause: Sentence A
quests.completedSentence: Compare: A) 'The horse racing down the track was disqualified.' B) 'The horse raced down the track was disqualified.' Which one means the horse itself was running?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Racing' (active) means the horse itself was running down the track. 'Raced' would suggest someone raced the horse, a less natural reading in this context.
quests.nativeTip: One participle shows the horse doing the running; the other would need someone racing the horse, which is a less natural reading here.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "Sentence A"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which is the correct reduced form of 'The workers who are striking for better pay have blocked the entrance'?
quests.targetClause: The workers striking for better pay have blocked the entrance.
quests.completedSentence: Which is the correct reduced form of 'The workers who are striking for better pay have blocked the entrance'?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Striking' correctly reduces 'who are striking,' dropping the pronoun and 'are.'
quests.nativeTip: Drop 'who are' and keep only the participle that matches the ongoing action.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The workers striking for better pay have blocked the entrance."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Which is the correct reduced form of 'The evidence that was presented in court convinced the jury'?
quests.targetClause: The evidence presented in court convinced the jury.
quests.completedSentence: Which is the correct reduced form of 'The evidence that was presented in court convinced the jury'?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Presented' correctly reduces 'that was presented,' dropping the pronoun and 'was,' matching the passive meaning.
quests.nativeTip: This clause is passive ('was presented') - which participle form matches that?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The evidence presented in court convinced the jury."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which is the correct reduced form of 'The book that my sister is reading was a birthday gift'?
quests.targetClause: This clause cannot be reduced to a participle phrase, because 'my sister,' not 'the book,' is doing the reading.
quests.completedSentence: Which is the correct reduced form of 'The book that my sister is reading was a birthday gift'?
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'my sister' - not 'the book' - is doing the reading, this is an object relative clause and cannot be reduced to a simple participle phrase attached to 'book.' Note: dropping 'that' to get 'the book my sister is reading' is a different technique - object relative pronoun omission - not participle reduction.
quests.nativeTip: Ask who is actually doing the reading - the book, or someone else mentioned in the clause?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "This clause cannot be reduced to a participle phrase, because 'my sister,' not 'the book,' is doing the reading."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Expand this reduced clause to its full form: 'The technicians repairing the server worked through lunch.'
quests.targetClause: The technicians who were repairing the server worked through lunch.
quests.completedSentence: Expand this reduced clause to its full form: 'The technicians repairing the server worked through lunch.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Repairing' most naturally expands to the past progressive 'who were repairing,' matching the ongoing nature of the action alongside 'worked through lunch.'
quests.nativeTip: The reduced participle 'repairing' suggests an ongoing action - which full verb tense best captures that?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The technicians who were repairing the server worked through lunch."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Expand this reduced clause to its full form: 'The applications submitted after the deadline were rejected automatically.'
quests.targetClause: The applications that were submitted after the deadline were rejected automatically.
quests.completedSentence: Expand this reduced clause to its full form: 'The applications submitted after the deadline were rejected automatically.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Submitted' expands to the passive 'that were submitted,' since applications are submitted by someone, not by themselves.
quests.nativeTip: 'Submitted' is a past participle - applications don't submit themselves, so which voice does the full clause need?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The applications that were submitted after the deadline were rejected automatically."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Expand this reduced clause to its full form, keeping the meaning and punctuation the same: 'The new policy, announced without warning, upset many employees.'
quests.targetClause: The new policy, which was announced without warning, upset many employees.
quests.completedSentence: Expand this reduced clause to its full form, keeping the meaning and punctuation the same: 'The new policy, announced without warning, upset many employees.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Announced' expands to 'which was announced,' and since this is non-defining information, both commas and 'which' (not 'that') must be used.
quests.nativeTip: Keep both commas exactly where they are, and choose the pronoun and voice that match the passive participle 'announced.'
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The new policy, which was announced without warning, upset many employees."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence correctly describes documents that SOMEONE ELSE reviewed, rather than documents that were reviewing anything?
quests.targetClause: The documents reviewed by the auditor revealed inconsistencies.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence correctly describes documents that SOMEONE ELSE reviewed, rather than documents that were reviewing anything?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Reviewed' (past participle) correctly shows the passive relationship: the auditor reviewed the documents. '-ing' would reverse the roles entirely.
quests.nativeTip: The documents didn't review anything themselves - someone reviewed them. Which participle shows this correctly?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The documents reviewed by the auditor revealed inconsistencies."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence correctly combines these facts, keeping the 'whose' clause intact: 'The novelist has a new book. The novelist's earlier work won critical acclaim. The novelist is currently touring five countries.'
quests.targetClause: The novelist, whose earlier work won critical acclaim, is currently touring five countries with a new book.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence correctly combines these facts, keeping the 'whose' clause intact: 'The novelist has a new book. The novelist's earlier work won critical acclaim. The novelist is currently touring five countries.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whose earlier work won critical acclaim' correctly keeps the possessive clause intact and unreduced, while the rest of the sentence combines the remaining facts clearly.
quests.nativeTip: The 'whose' clause must stay in full; only check whether the rest of the sentence is logically and grammatically combined.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The novelist, whose earlier work won critical acclaim, is currently touring five countries with a new book."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence contains an error related to reduced relative clauses?
quests.targetClause: The house who belonging to my uncle is for sale.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence contains an error related to reduced relative clauses?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The house who belonging to my uncle' incorrectly keeps 'who' alongside the reduced participle 'belonging'; a reduced clause never keeps its relative pronoun.
quests.nativeTip: A reduced clause drops its relative pronoun entirely - check whether any option has accidentally kept one.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The house who belonging to my uncle is for sale."
